incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for private-vpc-controlplane (severity: P1) -> Multiple connection failures from customer 'Acme Corp' to control plane endpoints. Rule: /private/controlplane/connection-loss.

pagerduty: Page details: incident_id=PD-48291, responders=oncall, escalation=network->platform.

Aisha K: acked. I'm pulling metrics and the control plane dashboard now.

Dan (oncall): on it. any customer impact indicators?

Aisha K: yes — TCP SYN retries from a subset of Acme's subnets to control-plane-01, and we see lots of ARP error counters on the edge NAT. Shards reporting increased connection churn.

Priya S: can you paste the host logs? might be agent flapping.

Aisha K: logs snippet from the private agent collector (tail):
```
2026-03-14T08:14:22Z agent: rx error: ARP timeout for 10.12.32.1
2026-03-14T08:14:23Z agent: connection to control-plane-01:443 failed: i/o timeout
2026-03-14T08:14:29Z agent: ARP retry count=5, flushing cache
2026-03-14T08:14:30Z kernel: Neighbor table: stale->failed for 10.12.32.1
```

Marco R: that looks like neighbor/ARP resolution failures in the customer's VPC. Could be a misbehaving router or host ARP storm.

Taylor (customer-acme): confirming, we saw intermittent failures across two subnets around 08:12-08:20 UTC, traffic drops ~30-45s, then recovers. No changes from our side.

Dan (oncall): preliminary impact: control plane requests from ~15% of Acme's instances are failing occasional RPCs; retries succeed but that increases latency and triggers client-side fallbacks. Not a full outage but customer-visible degradation.

Aisha K: quick mitigation options: 1) ask Acme to flush ARP caches or reboot affected hosts, 2) toggle agent's neighbor probing to aggressive (temporary), 3) route traffic through alternate AZ if available.

Priya S: runbook reference for "private agent connectivity loss" -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-agent-connectivity. Key steps: check neighbor table, sysctl arp_* values, increase agent keepalive, and engage network team.

Marco R: tagging network oncall. @Network Oncall can you confirm whether there are any recent route table updates or EC2 ENI flaps in the Acme account?

Network Oncall: saw brief ARP storms reported by fabric telemetry ~08:11-08:18 UTC correlated to host 10.12.32.1 in subnet-xx. Packet captures show repeated ARP requests for the same MAC that didn't get responses occasionally. No control plane fabric changes.

Dan (oncall): steps I'm doing now: 1) enable aggressive neighbor probing on the agent host (non-disruptive), 2) bump agent keepalive to 10s, 3) request customer to flush ARP cache on affected hosts. Will update.

Aisha K: command to aggressive probe (example for linux hosts):
```bash
# on affected host(s)
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh1=128
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh2=512
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh3=1024
# reduce NUD/arp timings
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.neigh.default.retrans_time_ms=100
```

Dan (oncall): applied neighbor tweaks to agent-proxy-7 in the customer's VPC. Watch logs.

Aisha K: agent-proxy-7 logs now show ARP retries reduced and successful re-resolves. latency back to baseline for that proxy.

Taylor (customer-acme): flushed ARP on a few hosts and saw immediate improvement. thanks.

Priya S: we should keep monitoring for 30m. also enable a temporary fallback route policy so if we see sustained ARP failures we route to control-plane-02 in a different AZ. That avoids repeated client retries.

Marco R: I'll open a follow-up to coordinate with infra/network to trace the failing switch/ENI. Also recommend running `tcpdump -i eth0 arp` on one affected host for 5m to capture the next event.

Dan (oncall): escalating to platform senior oncall per PD escalation (PD-48291 -> escalation to senior in 15m if any re-fires).

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: incident PD-48291 acknowledged by Dan (oncall). Next escalation at 2026-03-14T08:30:00Z if alert persists.

Aisha K: quick customer impact summary for notes: Acme Corp — partial connectivity degradation across two subnets, ~15% instance request failures, increased latency and retries. Workaround applied (neighbor tuning + ARP cache flush). Likely transient network/host-level ARP resolution issue, not Redwood control plane code bug.

Priya S: postmortem action items (preliminary): 1) add automatic agent neighbor-probe fallback for private deployments, 2) add runbook step to auto-request ARP cache flush via agent if permitted, 3) add per-customer ARP/neighbor telemetry to alert earlier.

Dan (oncall): handing off to Priya for follow-up and postmortem. I'll remain available for questions. :white_check_mark:

Priya S: taking it. will create incident record and schedule triage. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident PD-48291 status: acknowledged -> assigned (Priya S).

pagerduty: Incident PD-48291 status updated: resolved at 2026-03-14T09:02:34Z (root cause: transient ARP/neighbor resolution issues in customer VPC; mitigation: neighbor tuning + host ARP flush).

Taylor (customer-acme): confirmed resolved on our side. will follow up with our network team to find root cause. thx for the quick help. :pray:
